sources.entry: oneTBB - The shipping work-stealing runtime, arenas and task groups over a deque, the home of grain size and spin-before-sleep.

summary.one_liner: oneTBB is a C++ threading library from the UXL Foundation that lets you express logical parallelism through generic, template-based algorithms and tasks instead of managing threads directly.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes oneTBB as a flexible C++ library for adding parallelism to applications, aimed at multi-core performance and scalable, data-parallel programming. It lets you specify logical parallelism rather than threads, and is described as compatible with other threading packages. The README says usage is primarily through templates and generic programming. It points to a specification, a developer guide and reference, a migration guide from TBB, CMake and Bazel build notes, and WASM support. The README itself does not list specific algorithms, scheduler internals, or grain size and spin-before-sleep details, so those are not confirmed by this text.
use_cases: add multi-core parallelism to a C++ application
migrate legacy TBB code to oneTBB
build portable scalable C++ threaded code
compose parallel components in C++ programs
how_to_run: See Installation from Sources in the documentation to install oneTBB
Optionally use the CMake build system (see its README)
Optionally use basic Bazel build support
notable: Part of the UXL Foundation and an implementation of the oneAPI specification
Logical parallelism (tasks) rather than explicit threads
Successor to Threading Building Blocks (TBB), with a migration guide
Supports WASM builds per the README
caveats: The README is a high-level overview; details on platforms and requirements are deferred to separate release notes and system requirements docs
Work-stealing, grain size, and spin-before-sleep claims from the listing are not described in the README text
keywords: speed up c++ on multiple cores
